Each workstream lands as **one atomic commit** and is independently revertible.

## PHASE 2 — Failure-Mode Analysis

### System Assumptions

```text
Assumption 1 — Manifest completeness
Statement:  manifest.webmanifest is install-ready; the PWA gap is only the missing service worker.
Basis:      Discovery read of manifest.webmanifest (all required fields present).
Layer:      UI

Assumption 2 — Per-book stats are live
Statement:  SAVE.books[b] = {c, a} is maintained on every answer, so a weakness view
            needs no new tracking.
Basis:      js/game.js:1416 (`const b = SAVE.books[q.b] || {c:0,a:0}`) and panels.js:372 rows.
Layer:      UI / data

Assumption 3 — Ghost surface generalises
Statement:  upsertGhost/fetchGhosts accept a new mode value "live" with room-code run
            keys under existing RLS.
Basis:      Signatures take arbitrary strings; the rival feature already reads other
            users' rows.
Layer:      API Contract / Backend

Assumption 4 — Self-adjusting claim window
Statement:  The Judgement no-repeat window derives from the bank's false count, so bank
            growth is safe without retuning.
Basis:      tfPickClaim window formula (verified 2026-08-23).
Layer:      UI / logic

Assumption 5 — Node-only test gate
Statement:  All 47 suites are pure Node with no services or browsers, so CI needs only
            a Node runtime.
Basis:      test.js runner structure; every suite ran locally in this session.
Layer:      CI / Infra
```

### Failure Modes

```text
Failure Mode 1 — Stale cache after deploy
Layer:             UI / Infra
Description:       Service worker serves yesterday's index.html after a Vercel deploy;
                   players get old code indefinitely.
Trigger Condition: Any production deploy while an old SW controls the page.
Blast Radius:      Whole game silently frozen at an old version.
Mitigation:        sw.js uses network-first for the HTML shell and navigation requests,
                   a version-stamped cache name, skipWaiting+clientsClaim;
                   production-readiness test pins the network-first strategy.

Failure Mode 2 — Audio cache bloat
Layer:             Memory / Performance
Description:       Precaching ~30MB of soundtrack/voice exhausts mobile storage quota;
                   SW install fails or evicts arbitrarily.
Trigger Condition: SW install fetches audio/* on first visit.
Blast Radius:      Broken offline promise, storage errors on low-end devices.
Mitigation:        Audio is never precached — runtime cache-on-first-play with an LRU
                   trim (cap ~25 entries); test pins the exclusion.

Failure Mode 3 — CI Node mismatch
Layer:             Cross-layer
Description:       Workflow uses a Node version lacking syntax/APIs used by suites; CI
                   red on day one.
Trigger Condition: Default runner Node older than the features tests rely on.
Blast Radius:      The protection this workstream exists to provide never materialises.
Mitigation:        Pin node 20 LTS explicitly; Step 1 validation requires a green first
                   CI run (plus a deliberate red-run bootstrap check) before any other
                   workstream merges.

Failure Mode 4 — usedIds guard enables farming
Layer:             Logical
Description:       Skipping usedIds recording on zero-answer runs lets a player re-roll
                   a site's verse draw infinitely by quitting.
Trigger Condition: Guard keys only on attempts===0 while site stays uncleared.
Blast Radius:      Verse variety contract broken (same site re-drawn endlessly).
Mitigation:        Guard is exactly `R.attempts > 0` — any answered run still records;
                   fixes.test.js pins both branches.

Failure Mode 5 — Tier field breaks picker contracts
Layer:             Logical / Integration
Description:       Adding difficulty tiers to claims invalidates the existing
                   965-contract truefalse suite and picker weighting.
Trigger Condition: Tier-aware selection changes draw distribution.
Blast Radius:      47-suite gate goes red mid-program.
Mitigation:        Tiers are additive and optional: picker prefers arc-matched tier with
                   fallback to any tier; suite updated in the same step; marathon
                   regression re-run at the new bank size.

Failure Mode 6 — Mis-keyed context notes
Layer:             UI Contract
Description:       A note keyed by reference string attaches to the wrong verse (same
                   reference, different blank) and teaches error.
Trigger Condition: Duplicate references across core/extra packs.
Blast Radius:      Wrong doctrinal/explanatory text shown under a verse.
Mitigation:        Notes keyed by stable verseId() ids; a test resolves every note key
                   against BY_ID before shipping.

Failure Mode 7 — speechSynthesis unavailable
Layer:             UI
Description:       Listen-and-recite offered where TTS is missing; the mode is unplayable
                   (nothing to listen to).
Trigger Condition: Older browsers, or voice synthesis disabled.
Blast Radius:      Dead mode card, soft-lock risk if entered.
Mitigation:        Feature-detect on render; hide the toggle when unavailable; test pins
                   the guard.

Failure Mode 8 — Live-room rate/permissions failure
Layer:             Backend / API Contract
Description:       Per-question upserts plus polling hit Supabase limits, or RLS rejects
                   cross-user reads on the new mode value.
Trigger Condition: Room with several players; unexpected policy on unrecognized mode
                   strings.
Blast Radius:      Friend race silently empty or rate-limited.
Mitigation:        One upsert per question (10–20s cadence), poll ≥2.5s with an in-flight
                   guard; room falls back to the existing local/cloud rival when empty —
                   friend-race.test.js pins the fallback and cadence.

Failure Mode 9 — Artwork gate flipped early
Layer:             Process
Description:       asset-check flips to "required" before the 40 images exist; the suite
                   goes red and blocks everything.
Trigger Condition: Expectation change lands before binaries.
Blast Radius:      Whole 47-suite gate fails on missing files.
Mitigation:        Two-phase: prompts doc first; the expectation flip is the final step,
                   gated on asset-check reporting 0 missing.

Failure Mode 10 — Claim window math after growth
Layer:             Logical
Description:       Doubling the bank shifts the false-count-derived window; no-repeat or
                   weighting behaviour drifts.
Trigger Condition: Bank grows from 133 to ~280 claims.
Blast Radius:      Subtle Judgement balance regression nobody notices.
Mitigation:        Window formula self-derives (verified); the expanded suite re-asserts
                   marathon weighting and 40-draw no-repeat at the new size.
```

### Rollback Route

```text
ROLLBACK ROUTE:
- Precondition:       All 47 suites green at HEAD (verified 2026-08-23); each workstream
                      lands as ONE commit so reverts are atomic.
- Trigger:            If any step's named validation fails — specifically, if the full
                      suite (`node test.js`) goes red after a step's own validation —
                      execute `git revert` of that workstream's commit immediately,
                      before proceeding to any dependent step.

- UI:          [Undo] Revert the workstream commit; no UI state outlives the page session.
- Contract:    [No-op] No API contract is created or changed; nothing to revert.
- Backend:     [No-op] Supabase schema/policies untouched. Live-room rows are ordinary
                      user-scoped ghost data; they need no compensating transaction and
                      are keyed by room code (naturally abandoned).
- External:    [No-op] No destructive external effects. (CI workflow files are inert
                      until pushed.)
- Partial rollback:  Each workstream is independent; reverting one (e.g., the SW) never
                     requires reverting another (e.g., the claim bank).
- Verification:      After any revert, `node test.js` must report all suites passing and
                     `git status` must be clean.
```

### Execution Steps

#### Workstream 1 — CI protection

**Step 1: Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — on push/PR to master: checkout, setup Node 20, `npm test`. Include a one-time bootstrap check: push an intentionally failing commit on a scratch branch and confirm CI reports red, then remove it.
- Layer: CI/Infra · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: Green CI run on master executing all 47 suites; scratch-branch red run proves the gate actually gates.

#### Workstream 2 — Trust fix (the one real P0 left)

**Step 2: Guard `usedIds` recording in `js/results.js`** — where the run records the site's verse ids into the road (`recordSiteResult` path), pass the ids only when `R.attempts > 0`; a zero-answer quit must not spend the site's verses.
- Layer: UI/data · Dependencies: Step 1 (gate protects the fix)
- Validation: Quit a site brief without answering → next visit draws fresh verses; answer once → ids recorded as before.

**Step 3: Pin both branches in `test/fixes.test.js`** — static contracts: the `R.attempts > 0` guard exists; unconditional append removed.
- Layer: Test · Dependencies: Step 2
- Validation: `node test/fixes.test.js` passes; full suite green.

#### Workstream 3 — Judgement bank expansion + difficulty tiers

**Step 4: Expand `js/verses-tf.js`** from 133 to ~280 claims across all 40+ territory books, adding an optional tier field `t` (1 = familiar, 2 = subtle, 3 = deep-cut) to every claim; all existing authoring rules and scripture anchoring apply.
- Layer: Content · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: `node test/truefalse.test.js` count assertion raised; every new `why` carries a reference.

**Step 5: Tier-aware selection in `js/play.js` `tfPickClaim`** — prefer claims whose tier matches the site's arc position (Arc I–II → t1-weighted, III–IV → t2, V → t3), falling back to any tier; verdict weighting and the bounded window untouched.
- Layer: UI · Dependencies: Step 4
- Validation: Behavioral test draws from a t3-only site bias toward t3.

**Step 6: Update `test/truefalse.test.js`** — new count floor (≥250), tier field present on every claim, tier preference sanity, marathon regression and 40-draw no-repeat re-run at the new bank size.
- Layer: Test · Dependencies: Steps 4–5
- Validation: Suite passes; full run green.

#### Workstream 4 — PWA (installable + offline)

**Step 7: Create `sw.js`** — version-stamped cache; network-first for navigation/`index.html`; cache-first for CSS/JS/vendor/fonts; audio never precached, runtime cache-on-first-play with LRU trim (cap 25); `skipWaiting` + `clientsClaim`.
- Layer: UI/Infra · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: Serve locally; hard-reload then offline-reload renders the hall; second visit plays cached audio.

**Step 8: Register the worker in `index.html`** — guarded `if ('serviceWorker' in navigator)` registration after load.
- Layer: UI · Dependencies: Step 7
- Validation: SW active in DevTools; no double-registration warnings.

**Steps 9–10: Pin the contract in `test/production-readiness.test.js`** — asserts: registration snippet present; sw.js contains network-first for the shell, an explicit audio exclusion, a version-stamped cache name, and the LRU cap.
- Layer: Test · Dependencies: Steps 7–8
- Validation: Suite passes; full run green.

#### Workstream 5 — Learning loop

**Step 11: Create `js/verses-notes.js`** — one-line context notes (author, audience, occasion) keyed by stable `verseId()` ids for ~100 core verses; loaded as a content script with `module.exports` for tests.
- Layer: Content · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: Node script resolves every key against `BY_ID`.

**Step 12: Render notes in `js/results.js` (resolution line) and `js/panels.js` (Study Hall row)** where a note exists; plus the **thin-places section** in Study Hall — existing per-book accuracy rows sorted worst-first with a jump-to-practice action per book.
- Layer: UI (+ css/game.css styles) · Dependencies: Step 11
- Validation: A famous verse's results screen shows its note; Study Hall lists weakest books.

**Step 13: Listen-and-recite in `js/panels.js` + `js/play.js`** — a "Listen & Rebuild" study action: `speechSynthesis` speaks the full verse (rate ~0.9), then the existing typed-assembly flow runs; the option is hidden when TTS is unavailable.
- Layer: UI · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: With TTS present, flow completes and grades through the normal assembly path; with TTS absent, the action is not rendered.

**Step 14: Contracts in `test/production-readiness.test.js`** — note-key resolution against BY_ID; TTS feature-detect guard present; thin-places renders from `SAVE.books`.
- Layer: Test · Dependencies: Steps 11–13
- Validation: Full suite green.

#### Workstream 6 — Live friend races (MVP)

**Step 15: Room lifecycle in `js/cloud.js` + `js/game.js`** — "Race a Friend" from the hall: generate a 5-character room code; both players start the same site; each answer pushes a ghost sample via the **unchanged** `upsertGhost("live", code, score, timeline, meta)`; a 2.5s poll via `fetchGhosts("live", code, 5)` (in-flight guarded) renders the leader in the existing rival HUD; empty/failed rooms fall back to the standard rival.
- Layer: UI / API Contract (consumed) · Dependencies: Step 1
- Validation: Two browser profiles race the same site code; positions update without manual refresh; killing one player's network leaves the other's run intact.

**Step 16: Create `test/friend-race.test.js`** (registered as suite 48) — pins: mode value "live" used with room-code keys through the existing signatures; poll interval ≥2.5s with in-flight guard; rival fallback when the room is empty; no new Supabase surface referenced. Update counts in `test.js`, README, DEVELOPER-GUIDE.
- Layer: Test · Dependencies: Step 15
- Validation: 48/48 suites green.

#### Workstream 7 — Arc II–V artwork completion

**Step 17: Author `docs/reports/JOURNEY-ASSET-PROMPTS-ARC2-5.md`** — generation prompts for all 40 missing images following the established RIVAL-RACE-ASSET-PROMPTS pattern (style anchors, size, transparency), grouped by arc.
- Layer: Docs · Dependencies: NONE
- Validation: Every filename flagged by `node scripts/asset-check.js` has a corresponding prompt.

**Step 18: Process supplied art and flip the gate** — (user supplies generated images) run the existing `scripts/optimise-media.py` to WebP, then update `scripts/asset-check.js` from "missing is acceptable" to "required" **only once** the check reports 0 missing; extend its test contract in `test/production-readiness.test.js`.
- Layer: Infra/Test · Dependencies: Step 17 + user-supplied binaries
- Validation: `node scripts/asset-check.js` → 0 missing; full suite green.

## PHASE 4 — Adversarial Audit

```text
[✓] 1. BOUNDARY COMPLIANCE
    Challenge: Find any action that touches a file outside MODIFIABLE FILES.

    supabase/, bank, vendor untouched.

    mode and mitigation rather than silent trust.

[✓] 4. STEP VALIDATION COMPLETENESS
    Challenge: A validation that could pass without the step's goal achieved.

    asset-check output, not file presence; behavioral validations exercise both
    branches (quit-fresh vs answered-recorded; TTS present vs absent).

[✓] 5. ROLLBACK VIABILITY
    Challenge: A fired trigger whose undo cannot restore prior state.
    Justification: Every workstream is one atomic commit; SW has no external state;
    room rows are ordinary user data needing no compensation; no irreversible step
    exists in the plan.

[✓] 6. SCOPE DISCIPLINE
    Challenge: Behaviour changes beyond the stated problem.
    Justification: Notes render only where they exist; tiers act only inside
    tfPickClaim; standard mechanics untouched; the already-fixed daily P0 is explicitly
    dropped rather than re-touched.

[✓] 7. WORKFLOW COMPLETENESS
    Challenge: A declared layer with no execution step.
    Justification: UI — Steps 2, 5, 7–8, 11–13, 15; API Contract — Step 15 consumes the
    existing contract unchanged (deviation from contract-first justified: no new
    contract exists to define); Backend — unchanged by design, documented not silent;
    Test — Steps 1, 3, 6, 9–10, 14, 16, 18; CI/Infra — Step 1.

[✓] 8. CONTRACT CONSISTENCY
    Challenge: A field, type, or shape mismatch between UI sends and backend expects.
    Justification: Step 15 reuses upsertGhost/fetchGhosts verbatim with mode "live" and
    room-code keys; timeline samples keep the {t, p} shape the rival HUD already
    renders; no new field names exist to mismatch.
```
